2. It is true that under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and section 24 of the non-Agricultural Tenancy Act a case for preemption can only be instituted after the transfer of the disputed land i. e. after the completion of the registration of the deed of sale as contemplated under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act read with section, 61 of the Registration Act. It is also equally true that a suit for preemption under Muslim Law can only be instituted after the execution and registration of the document of sale as contemplated under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act read with section 61 of the Registration Act However, under the Muslim Law of the redemption before a suit for preemption is instituted the preemptor must make a demand for preemption immediately after the sale. Article 236 of Chapter XIII at page 272 of Mullah's Mohammadan Law, 18th Edition states that no person is entitled to the right of redemption's unless he has declared his intention to assert the right immediately on receiving information of the sale. This formality is called Talab-i-Mowasibat i. e. the immediate demand by jumping. The question is for the purpose of making Talab-i-Mowasibat i. e. the first demand for pre-emption, when the sale of the property in question shall be deemed to be complete whether on the completion of all formalities as contemplated under section 54 of the Transfer Property Act read with section 61 of the Registration not or on pavement of price and delivery possession of the property. In this connection it may be mentioned that so far as Muslim Law it concerned admittedly there is no obligatory provision for execution and registration of a document for the purpose of sale of any immoveable property. Thus the question is whether the first demand for preemption by way of Talabi Mowasibat can be made on the completion of the sale of a Property under the customary Muslim Law. i. e. after the payment of price and delivery of possession of the properly or it can be made after the completion of the sale as contemplated under the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act and Registration Act. This question has assumed an importance in view of certain recent decisions of tie Indian Supreme Court, wherein the established principle that followed for near a century has been overruled. The Supreme Court of India has now ruled that a Talab-i-Mowasibat can only be made after the completion of registration of the deed of sale as contemplated under section 61 of the Registration Act. If these decisions are accepted as such it must be held that the demand for preemption in the present case is definitely prematured being admittedly made before the registration of the deed of sale as contemplated under section 61 of the Registration Act. It is to be considered hereinafter whether such decision of the Supreme Court of India are to be accepted as reported in AIR 1960 (SC) 1368, AIR 1961 (SC) 1747 and AIR 1972 (SC) 2162. 

 "It seems to us that a strict compliance with all the requirements of the two demands which are necessary before a pre-emptor can succeed in a suit for preemption under the Muhammedan Law may become very difficult, particularly, on the question of the promptness and avoidance of delay with regard to the first demand. As stated before a sale shall be deemed to be completed only after the sale deed has been copied in the books of the Sub-Registrar. If the demand has to be made after such completion it would be virtually impossible or at any rate extremely difficult for any pre-emptor to make the first demand as promptly as required under the principles of Muhammedan Law. It cannot be expected that a preemptor should keep a perpetual watch and go on making constant inquiries with regard to the point of time when the office of the Sub Registrar would copy out the sale deed in the prescribed book. However that is a matter on which legislation my become necessary and that is for the parliament to consider and not for us." 

 10. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated hereinbefore the judgment of the trial Court granting preemption against appellant is upheld and confirm. This appeal is accordingly dismissed. But in the facts of this case there will be no order as to costs.
